info.name: Riverbend work orders API
info.description:
Every endpoint of the Riverbend API, in the order a message flows through the system. Pick an environment (local or GCP), then run the folders top to bottom: later requests use ids saved by earlier ones. Step-by-step code walkthrough for each request: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md.

Three credentials: X-Ingest-Key (the email gateway); Bearer staff credentials, either a personal session token from signing in with email and password or a shop's static token; Bearer admin token. The customer's reply token is in their link.

item.name: 0. Health
item.description: No auth. Used by load balancers and the console's connection check.

request.description:
Is the process up? Never touches the database.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#healthz

Can it reach the database? Also says which model provider this deployment runs.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#readyz

item.name: 1. Sign in (staff)
item.description: A staff token is bound to exactly one shop.

item.name: Sign in with email and password

request.description:
How a person signs in. Returns a personal session token that opens the account's shops and expires (12 h by default). Saves it into {{sessionToken}}.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#login

exec: pm.test('a person, not a shop token', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().account).to.be.an('object'));

request.description:
The same endpoint the console uses, with the session token: returns the account and every shop it opens.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#me

item.name: Who am I (a shop's static token)

request.description:
The console signs in with only a token: this says which shop it belongs to, and which optional features this deployment has. Saves shop_id into {{shopId}}.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#me

Wrong password and unknown email get the same answer. Five wrong passwords in a row lock the account for 15 minutes (429), so don't run this five times on GCP.

Expected: HTTP 401. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#login

item.name: 2. Intake: the email gateway
item.description: How a customer's email reaches the system. Auth: X-Ingest-Key.

request.description:
What the email gateway sends for every inbound email. Returns 202 at once; the AI runs later in the worker. message_id is the idempotency key (the email's Message-ID).

Expected: HTTP 202. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#inbound

body.raw:
{
  "message_id": "{{gatewayMessageId}}",
  "channel": "email",
  "received_at": "{{receivedAt}}",
  "sender": "Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@example.com>",
  "body": "Hi, my rear brake squeals and the chain is rusty. Can I bring it in Thursday morning? Sam"
}

request.description:
Gateways retry. Same message_id + same body = 200 with duplicate=true and the same ids; nothing is stored twice and the customer gets no second acknowledgement.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#inbound

body.raw:
{
  "message_id": "{{gatewayMessageId}}",
  "channel": "email",
  "received_at": "{{receivedAt}}",
  "sender": "Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@example.com>",
  "body": "Hi, my rear brake squeals and the chain is rusty. Can I bring it in Thursday morning? Sam"
}

request.description:
A reused message_id with a different body is a gateway bug: 409, nothing stored.

Expected: HTTP 409. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#inbound

Missing or unknown X-Ingest-Key: 401.

Expected: HTTP 401. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#inbound

body.raw:
{
  "message_id": "{{gatewayMessageId}}",
  "channel": "email",
  "received_at": "{{receivedAt}}",
  "sender": "Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@example.com>",
  "body": "Hi, my rear brake squeals and the chain is rusty. Can I bring it in Thursday morning? Sam"

item.name: 3. Staff: send a message as a customer (test tool)
item.description: Staff try the whole workflow without an email gateway. Own shop only. Off in production unless TEST_MESSAGES=true (the GCP demo has it on).

request.description:
Goes through the same intake as a real email. No day is given, so the AI asks one follow-up question. Saves {{conversationId}} and {{customerId}}.

Expected: HTTP 202. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#test-messages

exec: // Give the background worker time to process the previous message.

reply_to continues the conversation (it looks up the conversation's reply token for you). The AI now has a problem and a day: a work order is created.

Expected: HTTP 202. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#test-messages

item.name: Customer asks about the finished order (goes to staff)

exec: // Give the background worker time to process the previous message.

request.description:
The conversation already has a work order, so the model is not asked: it goes straight to a person and the customer gets a 'passed to the team' note.

Expected: HTTP 202. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#test-messages

item.name: 4. Staff: inbox and conversations
item.description: Everything that is not (yet) a work order.

exec: // Give the background worker time to process the previous message.

request.description:
In flight, waiting for the customer, held at the cap, or waiting for a person. needs_action=true is the red badge in the console.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#inbox

Messages both ways, the timeline of events, and every model call with its cost. The reply token is never returned.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#conversation

Goes out through the outbox. A conversation waiting for a person goes back to 'work order created' (or 'answered' when it has no order). resolved=true says so.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#reply

Same client_id = the same reply: duplicate=true, nothing new is sent.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#reply

item.name: Retry the AI (only after a failure)

request.description:
Re-queues a message the AI gave up on (dead) or that was held at the cap (parked). On a healthy conversation there is nothing to retry: 409.

Expected: HTTP 409. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#retry

Open and cancel-requested orders, oldest first, with the total of open estimates. Saves the test customer's order into {{workOrderId}}.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#work-orders

Also completed and cancelled ones.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#work-orders

The ticket: bike, issues, priced lines, estimate, requested window, review flags.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#work-order

Staff change the status: open, completed or cancelled. Recorded on the timeline.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#work-order-status

Everyone who wrote from an email address, most recently active first.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#customers

Every conversation, every message both ways, and every event, in one timeline.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#customer

Every call to the model, including failed and rejected ones, with tokens and cost.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#llm-calls

The shop's timeline: received, asked, created, escalated, held, ...

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#activity

The monthly cap, spent, reserved (calls in flight) and remaining.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#spend

item.name: 8. Customer side (needs the reply token)
item.description: The customer's link carries an unguessable reply token. No staff API returns it (by design). Locally, read it from the database: psql postgresql://postgres@localhost:5433/riverbend -c "SELECT reply_token FROM conversations WHERE id = '<gatewayConversationId>'" and paste it into {{replyToken}}.

exec: // Give the background worker time to process the previous message.

request.description:
Only the messages we sent them, and a plain-language status. No auth: the token is the key.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#customer-view

item.name: Customer replies by email (gateway, with reply token)

request.description:
The gateway passes the token from our reply-to address, so the reply lands in the same conversation. This one already has a work order, so it goes to a person.

Expected: HTTP 202. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#inbound

body.raw:
{
  "message_id": "{{gatewayReplyId}}",
  "channel": "email",
  "received_at": "{{receivedAt}}",
  "sender": "Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@example.com>",
  "reply_token": "{{replyToken}}",
  "body": "Thanks! Can you also check the tyre pressure?"
}

request.description:
Which model this process uses and whether the circuit breaker is open.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#admin-provider

item.name: Set a shop's monthly AI cap

request.description:
Changes the cap. Raising it releases messages held at the cap. CAREFUL on GCP: this changes the live shop's cap.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#admin-budget

Everyone who can sign in: shops, disabled or locked, open sessions, last sign-in. Never a password or hash.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#admin-staff

There is no self sign-up: an admin creates each person's account. The email here is unique per run. Give the person their password; they can change it from the console.

Expected: HTTP 201. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#admin-staff

Disabling signs the person out everywhere at once; so does setting a new password. Other fields: name, shops, password.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#admin-staff

item.description: Exist only when DEV_MODE=true. 404 on GCP.

request.description:
The local dashboard's credentials and provider state. Never available in production.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#dev
Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#dev

Every model call now fails. Send a message and watch it get retried, then handed to staff.

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#dev

Expected: HTTP 200. Code walkthrough: docs/API_WALKTHROUGH.md#dev

exec: (err, res) => pm.test('the signed-out token is refused', () => pm.expect(res.code).to.eql(401)));
